text:
redirect. The post's own diagram draws, but wrongly: the flowchart renderer drops the edge whose label is a picture link and repeats the shared node 4 times; launch one fix step for `renderMermaidBlock` with this post as its test case.

Cross review (owner's rule of 2026-11-26): CL36, CL38, CL39 and CL40 together. One comment under each; this one is CL36's.

## Holds
- Checks rerun on main at 75d5fac: `tests.test_cl36_post_body` **7 of 7 OK**; `node kit/board/test_page_body.js` **all passed** (phone and desktop).
- **What he asked, on the real thing** ("Why is your flowchart just code then?"): I opened this post on the local board page at 390 px with touch (`scripts/review/CR-cl38-attaching-repos-on-the-web-install-py-al-cl36-diagram.js`). Good: the flowchart is no longer code (0 `flowchart LR` code blocks), the inline picture loads (1280 px natural, 345 px wide on the phone), nothing is wider than the screen (390).
- **But the diagram is not this post's diagram.** The source has 6 nodes and 5 edges into one hub. The page draws a single column of 8 boxes: "Part's result, Post body, Post body, Owner reads one place, ```mermaid block, Post body, docs/X.md § Section embeds only, Post body". "Post body" appears **4 times** (measured), and the edge `E["![picture](repo/path.png)"] --> B` is **missing**: the picture input, the very thing CL36 added, is not on the diagram. The renderer lists edges one after another; it does not draw a graph, and a label holding `![..](..)` is lost.
- Smaller, same screen: the four-backtick inline code (```` ```mermaid ````) in the table and in "The rule" shows as broken backtick fragments, and the table's "now" column is cut at the phone width (scrolls inside).
- The test passes because it checks that a diagram is drawn, not that each node is drawn once and every edge is there. A check that never saw this fail holds nothing for it.
- Not checked: the published Artifact page (same `shim.js`), a real phone.

## Goal (the train, read across CL36, CL38, CL39, CL40)
- The `cli` train serves one thing here: **the owner never types in chat; the board and the repo are the only places things are said, once.** CL38 started as "allow add_repo"; the owner refused that ("Yours of getting the user to write in chat isn't one"), so CL38 became "parts never attach, messages are 200-char pointers", CL39 "one web environment holding every repo, hooks at user level", CL40 "launch a step from a read-only clone". Three steps on one problem: getting a second repo into a web session without the owner.
- The measure each step used is a stand-in: fixture tests (a bare remote with a pre-receive hook for CL40, a "Harmonize-shaped" scratch copy for CL39). The real thing is Harmonize, and K2 says the orchestrator runs it.
- What the posts show together that no single one says: **every one of the three ends with the Harmonize run handed to the orchestrator, and only CL38's was ever recorded.** CL39 and CL40 have no `real_project` (checked in their posts today, 3 days after Done); the question post `KIT-web-env` does not exist on the board; Harmonize's `env_01VxiCbR...` is not recorded with `kit.py web-env --id`. So the chain's end state (an orchestrator started by the kit in that environment, launching a step with nothing typed) has never run once.
- The owner last tried this chain himself on 11-24 (his comments under CL36 and CL38). Since then he is using the board daily (comments up to 11-27 02:31, on other trains), but not this result. More than three Dones without his try: the next step is that try, and it needs the two K2 runs first.

## Not checked
- Harmonize itself (not attached in this review session): its committed `install.py --update`, the env id, its orchestrator-handoff skill edit (CL40's handoff).
- A real refused push (CL40) and a real container built by CL39's setup script.
- The published Artifact page (I checked the local board page, which uses the same `shim.js` renderer).
